items.title: $N=2$ central-charge saturation is equivalent to annihilation by the null supercharge pair
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft with complete conditional argument or definition; current prerequisite interfaces and page inventories reconciled in the owner resolution evidence. Root records readiness separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Use the four-dimensional rigid $N=2$ super-Poincare convention with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\epsilon_{12}=1$, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$. Let $\mathcal K\ne\{0\}$ be a positive Hilbert rest-fiber representation with $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$, $M>0$, scalar central charges $Z^{12}=zI$ and $Z^{21}=-zI$, and a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$ on which the supercharges, their actual Hilbert adjoints, and every product below are defined. Thus $P_0=-M$, each supercharge has mass dimension one-half, and $M,z$ have mass dimension one. If $z\ne0$, set $\omega=z/|z|$; if $z=0$, set $\omega=1$. Then $|\omega|=1$ and $\overline{\omega} z=|z|$ by the central-charge theorem. On $\mathcal D$ put

$$q=Q^1_1,\qquad r=Q^2_2,\qquad A=q-\omega r^*,\qquad A^\sharp=q^*-\overline{\omega}r.$$

For every $\psi\in\mathcal D$,

$$\langle(AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A)\psi,\psi\rangle=\|A\psi\|^2+\|A^\sharp\psi\|^2=4(M-|z|)\|\psi\|^2.$$

Consequently, for every nonzero $\psi\in\mathcal D$, $M=|z|$ if and only if $A\psi=A^\sharp\psi=0$. The operator $A^\sharp$ is the displayed sum of the individual charge adjoints; for unbounded charges it is not asserted to be the maximal-domain adjoint of the sum $A$. This conditional statement neither asserts that such a vector or representation occurs in a physical model nor proves its dynamical stability.

items.title: BPS state and central-charge saturation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft with complete conditional argument or definition; current prerequisite interfaces and page inventories reconciled in the owner resolution evidence. Root records readiness separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and use natural units $\hbar=c=1$. Let $N\ge2$, and let a selected four-dimensional rigid super-Poincare representation have a nonzero Hilbert space with positive inner product, future-cone joint momentum spectrum, and closed supercharges with actual Hilbert adjoints on the common invariant product domain specified here. A **massive rest fiber** is a nonzero Hilbert space $\mathcal K$ carrying the restricted supercharge and central-charge operators on a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$, with $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$, $M>0$, and scalar central-charge matrix $Z=(z^{IJ})$ acting by $Z^{IJ}=z^{IJ}I$, where $z^{IJ}=-z^{JI}$. Use metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so $P_0=-M$, and the convention $\epsilon_{12}=1$ in the supercharge algebra.

For $v\in\mathbb C^N$, set $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_I|v_I|^2$ and define $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Zv\|_2$. The unitary massive-fiber bound is $M\ge\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. A **BPS-saturated state** in this item is a nonzero vector $\psi\in\mathcal D$ in a specified massive rest fiber for which $M=\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. This term records algebraic saturation only; it does not assert that any specified charge is represented by a state, or that a saturating state exists, is stable, or occurs in a physical spectrum.

For $N=2$, write $z=z^{12}$, so $Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|z|$. If $z\ne0$, set $\omega=z/|z|$; if $z=0$, set $\omega=1$. The central-charge theorem gives $|\omega|=1$ and $\overline{\omega} z=|z|$. Define $A=Q^1_1-\omega(Q^2_2)^*$ and $A^\sharp=(Q^1_1)^*-\overline{\omega}Q^2_2$ on $\mathcal D$. In this $N=2$ case, a nonzero domain vector saturates the bound if and only if both displayed combinations annihilate it. For unbounded charges, $A^\sharp$ denotes the displayed sum of individual adjoints and is not assumed to be the maximal-domain adjoint of $A$.

items.title: Finite $N=2$ rest-fiber algebra at central-charge saturation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft with complete conditional argument or definition; current prerequisite interfaces and page inventories reconciled in the owner resolution evidence. Root records readiness separately.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and let $\mathcal K$ have orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle,|2\rangle,|12\rangle$. Give $\mathcal K$ the grading for which $|0\rangle,|12\rangle$ are even and $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ are odd. Define operators $c_1,c_2$ by

$$c_1|0\rangle=0,\quad c_1|1\rangle=|0\rangle,\quad c_1|2\rangle=0,\quad c_1|12\rangle=|2\rangle,$$

$$c_2|0\rangle=0,\quad c_2|1\rangle=0,\quad c_2|2\rangle=|0\rangle,\quad c_2|12\rangle=-|1\rangle,$$

and let $c_1^\dagger,c_2^\dagger$ be their actual Hilbert adjoints. Set

$$Q^1_1=\sqrt{2M}\,c_1,\quad Q^2_2=\sqrt{2M}\,c_1^\dagger,\quad Q^1_2=\sqrt{2M}\,c_2,\quad Q^2_1=-\sqrt{2M}\,c_2^\dagger.$$

Take $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$, $Z^{12}=M I$, $Z^{21}=-M I$, $Z^{11}=Z^{22}=0$, and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}=(Q^I_\alpha)^\dagger$. On $\mathcal D=\mathcal K$ these matrices satisfy the massive $N=2$ rest-frame supercharge relations with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\epsilon_{12}=1$. The central-charge bound is saturated and the corresponding combination $A=Q^1_1-(Q^2_2)^\dagger$ vanishes identically. This is a finite-dimensional module for the rest-frame supercharge algebra; no extension to the full Poincare group or physical particle is asserted.

items.title: Finite $N=2$ rest-fiber algebra with zero central charge and strict bound
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft with complete conditional argument or definition; current prerequisite interfaces and page inventories reconciled in the owner resolution evidence. Root records readiness separately.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and let $\mathcal K=\Lambda\mathbb C^4$ with orthonormal basis $|S\rangle$ indexed by subsets $S\subseteq\{1,2,3,4\}$ and grading $(-1)^{|S|}$. For $j\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ define $c_j|S\rangle=0$ when $j\notin S$ and
$c_j|S\rangle=(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s<j\}|}|S\setminus\{j\}\rangle$ when $j\in S$. Let $c_j^\dagger$ be the actual Hilbert adjoint. For $I,\alpha\in\{1,2\}$ put $j=2(I-1)+\alpha$ and set $Q^I_\alpha=\sqrt{2M}\,c_j$, with $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}=(Q^I_\alpha)^\dagger$. Take $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$ and $Z^{IJ}=0$. On $\mathcal D=\mathcal K$, these operators satisfy the massive $N=2$ rest-frame supercharge relations with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\epsilon_{12}=1$. Since $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=0<M$, the central-charge bound is strict in these rest-frame algebra data, so the mass/central-charge equality condition for BPS saturation is not met. This finite module is a representation of the rest-frame supercharge algebra only; it is not asserted to extend to a full Poincare representation or a physical particle.

references.title: Adel Bilal, Introduction to Supersymmetry
references.locator: §3.4, printed pp. 13–15 (PDF pp. 18–20), massive central-charge oscillator algebra and the distinction between strict and saturated bounds.

references.locator: §2.4.2, printed pp. 40–41 (PDF pp. 31–32), long versus short massive N=2 representations; the finite CAR module is constructed locally.
